text.text: MMseqs2, three rounds
A profile of a protein family, built by MMseqs2 from its own hits over three rounds of search, as jackhmmer does.
Will it work for you?

Is the closest same-family domain in the relative you will search at least 40% identical, for most of your proteins? If yes, Fmax here is 40–60% 0.241 (n = 563), 60–100% 0.300 (n = 1,289). If no, 20–30% 0.337 (n = 93), 30–40% 0.209 (n = 165). (Pfam truth set, raw calls, zebrafish (435 Mya) as the relative searched, setting sensitivity 7, 3 rounds; subsets with at least 30 true instances.)

Are the features you care about longer than 60 residues? If yes, Fmax here is 61–120 aa 0.245 (n = 963), 121–250 aa 0.319 (n = 504), 251 aa or more 0.462 (n = 277). If no, 16–30 aa 0.028 (n = 271), 31–60 aa 0.085 (n = 420). (Pfam truth set, raw calls, zebrafish (435 Mya) as the relative searched, setting sensitivity 7, 3 rounds.)
Can you spend about 0.0787 core-hours per 1,000 proteins for each relative you search? That is the measured mean per relative; see "Cost per 1,000 queries" below.
Best Fmax and cost

Under the Pfam truth set, raw calls, zebrafish (435 Mya) as the relative searched, its best setting is sensitivity 7, 3 rounds (s7): Fmax 0.324 over 2,435 true instances. Searching costs about $0.00351 per 1,000 queries (0.0787 core-hours), for each relative searched.
Where it is strong and weak

Each line compares this setting with the best setting of any other tool on the same subset of the proteins, so the other tool's setting can change from line to line. Only subsets with at least 30 true instances are compared.
Where it is closest to, or furthest ahead of, the best other tool:
identity 30–40% to the closest same-family domain: Fmax 0.209 (n = 165); best other: phmmer, default options, 0.199.
AlphaFold confidence (pLDDT) 90–100: Fmax 0.484 (n = 186); best other: MMseqs2, sensitivity 7, 0.480.
Where it is furthest behind the best other tool:
regions 16–30 aa long: Fmax 0.028 (n = 271); best other: kmerseek, wwmj5, k = 11, 0.330.
regions 31–60 aa long: Fmax 0.085 (n = 420); best other: kmerseek, gbmr4, k = 21, 0.232.
Swiss-Prot features, raw calls, zebrafish, setting sensitivity 7, 3 rounds: best feature type domain, Fmax 0.321 (n = 1,107); worst short motif, Fmax 0.004 (n = 190).

Figure 2. Where MMseqs2, three rounds is ahead and behind: its Fmax on each subset of the proteins, against the best other tool on that subset (Pfam truth set, raw calls, zebrafish as the relative; its best setting, sensitivity 7, 3 rounds). Left out, under 30 true instances: 0–20%.
What it compares
A profile of a protein family, built by MMseqs2 from its own hits over three rounds of search, as jackhmmer does.
What it needs
sequence only: yes
3D structure prediction: no
GPU: no
Reference searched
The relative's proteome (Quest for Orthologs reference proteomes, release 2020_04), as an MMseqs2 database.
How to read its score
Bit score: higher ranks first. The E-value cutoff was 10.
Known failure modes
At most 1,000 target proteins are kept per query (--max-seqs 1000). How often that cut hits: not measured.
Each round can pull in proteins from a different family. How often: not measured.
Cost per 1,000 queries

Setting s7, searching one relative (mean over the 15 relatives it searched): 0.0787 core-hours reserved per 1,000 queries (16 cores for the task's wall time), measured on Sherlock. Peak memory 1.1 GB. That is about $0.00351 at $0.044625 per CPU-hour. Building its databases took 0.00889 core-hours over 7 databases. A database is built once and reused, so this is not in the per-query cost. This covers the 7 database builds the task records hold; the search used 15 relatives.
The per-query cost counts the search only. The run recorded cost per tool and setting, summed over all relatives, so the cost for one relative is the mean.

Settings in the table
sensitivity 7, 3 rounds (s7): sensitivity 7 (-s 7), three rounds
Version, container, command
Version: MMseqs2 18.8cc5c
Container: quay.io/biocontainers/mmseqs2:18.8cc5c--hd6d6fdc_0 (sha256:3503bfe576d560e550df2872af86a1ad1bcc1c06cfb7caadd3e7a95649f5f0ef)
mmseqs search \ human-38fdd87d_mmdb/db zebrafish_mmdb/db result mmseqs_tmp \ --threads 16 \ -s 7 \ --num-iterations 3 \ --max-seqs 1000 \ -e 10.0
Followed by mmseqs convertalis to write the table of hits.
